title: NOUNS AFTER HOURS — Entertainment Development
status: Proposed formats and internal planning estimates; no attachment, commission, distribution agreement or talent endorsement.

audience.primary: People who live with screens and still want things made by hand: young adult and adult animation viewers, creative workers, design and independent-comics audiences.
audience.secondary: Nouns and bot-companion communities, paper collectors, small event hosts, animation festivals and art-book audiences.
audience.entryPoint: You do not need to know crypto or use an AI bot. The entry is ten personalities trying to make a place feel like home.
audience.emotionalOffer: A comedy about usefulness, friendship and the parts of life that cannot be optimized.

treatments.title: The Midnight Shift
treatments.logline: One useful companion trait, one small nighttime problem, one practical visual joke that becomes a real feeling.
treatments.treatment: Each short begins on a familiar desktop. Midnight opens a door into Offscreen. A companion attempts to solve an ordinary cinema problem using their daytime specialty: a checklist for belonging, a timetable for spontaneity, a ranking for which door to open. The first minute escalates a readable prop gag. The second gives the character a small relational choice and a warm comic button. The last five seconds reveal an art note from the night. Episodes work alone; the ten reverses form the finale sentence.
treatments.visualApproach: Limited 2D animation using unchanged original Noun portraits, moving props, holds, camera moves and expressive typography. One recurring environment keeps production bounded.
treatments.pilot: Clocking Out: Desk Buddy’s smallest unfinished task is simply sitting down with someone.
treatments.audienceUse: Native short-form video, an owned-site player, festival or exhibition interstitials. Distribution is proposed, not secured.

treatments.title: The Between
treatments.format: 10 × approximately 11-minute animated episodes, adaptable from the ten comics
treatments.logline: Ten task companions inherit the night shift at a neighborhood cinema, where the hardest job is making room for each other.
treatments.treatment: The eleven-minute format adds an A-story and a light B-story while preserving one character spotlight. The A-story follows a practical obstacle to reopening the cinema. The B-story pairs two other companions whose habits create a contrasting joke. These strands meet in a live program, a physical repair or a shared choice. The season has a simple engine—one midnight-to-dawn shift per episode—and a finite first objective: open The Between. After opening, the building becomes an expandable venue for guests, neighborhood mysteries and original genre nights.
treatments.pilot: Clocking Out becomes an ensemble introduction: Desk Buddy and Relay discover The Between while Keeper and Scout investigate the cabinet of unissued notes.

pilotBeatSheet.name: The last checkbox
pilotBeatSheet.action: A completed daytime checklist feels oddly empty. Midnight turns the companion window into a door.

pilotBeatSheet.name: Offscreen
pilotBeatSheet.action: Desk Buddy and Relay follow an EXIT arrow to a cinema with no title on its marquee.

pilotBeatSheet.name: Open for what?
pilotBeatSheet.action: They find the brass instruction plate and a box of mismatched chairs. Desk Buddy makes a three-step reopening plan.

pilotBeatSheet.name: The cabinet
pilotBeatSheet.action: Keeper and Scout discover incomplete paper editions. Their smallest clue is a blank rectangle where the reason for the event should be.

pilotBeatSheet.name: The useful montage
pilotBeatSheet.action: Each companion applies a specialty. Posters proliferate, schedules compress and invitations require invitations.

pilotBeatSheet.name: Ready for nobody
pilotBeatSheet.action: The room is technically ready. Every chair faces a wall because the seating chart was beautifully wrong.

pilotBeatSheet.name: A smaller opening
pilotBeatSheet.action: Harbor asks where the helpers will sit. Desk Buddy realizes the plan never included them.

pilotBeatSheet.name: The first program
pilotBeatSheet.action: Tempo’s projector stalls; Muse makes a shadow with a paper cup. The accidental shadow becomes a show.

pilotBeatSheet.name: Attendance of two, company of ten
pilotBeatSheet.action: The ten gather in small pairs around the changing shadows. Desk Buddy leaves the fourth checkbox blank on purpose.

pilotBeatSheet.name: A beginning
pilotBeatSheet.action: Treasury prints the first art note, labeled 1 BEGINNING. Its reverse reads A. Dawn returns them to their windows. Desk Buddy adds a new personal line: Come back.

treatments.title: Open for What? A Night at The Between
treatments.format: A 45–60-minute live illustrated comedy and print exhibition
treatments.logline: A miniature cinema is built in front of the audience while its very helpful hosts keep discovering what they forgot to leave room for.
treatments.treatment: A host welcomes visitors into an intentionally unfinished cinema. Short projected comic scenes alternate with live paper-folding, an original sound loop and dry prop comedy. Guests may dedicate a card, leave a seat open or make a paper shadow; participation always has a watching-only option. The final sequence combines their voluntary contributions into one temporary wall. The take-home object is an art note or mini-comic, never a promise of financial value. The show ends by turning the empty marquee into OPEN FOR EACH OTHER.
spatialPlan: Entry: one restrained poster and a clearly marked welcome desk.
Middle: three folding tables, ten character cards and a small original-art display.
Stage: a simple screen, live camera for paper actions and movable chairs.
Exit: free viewing of the complete ten-issue sequence; any paid merchandise clearly separated from participation.

excluded: Insurance, accessibility provision or licenses beyond the eventual event-specific scope

creatorStatement: I want to make companions that have a life beyond the task. Nouns After Hours treats a small printed object, a good joke and a place to sit as serious creative material. The ambition is an original entertainment world that can live on a screen, in a comic, on a shirt and in a room full of people. — Michael Hoydich
packagingAngles: Animation: a bounded recurring set and ten distinct comic engines support an ensemble series.
Independent cinema: a love letter to small venues, paper ephemera and imperfect shared experiences.
Design culture: physical posters and art notes are story objects rather than added merchandise.
Live culture: an exhibition can become an evening with a beginning, a joke, participation and an ending.
rightsAndProductionNotes: Underlying original Nouns artwork is CC0; preserve the actual source provenance. New scripts, music, performances, layouts and production agreements need their own documented terms.
Budget ranges are internal working estimates as of 19 October 2026, created for scope discussion. Obtain project-specific quotes before commissioning.
No actor, filmmaker, agency, studio, platform or distributor has endorsed or joined this project in this kit.
When pitching, use original genre references and production language rather than imitation celebrity casting or franchise promises.
